acceptance_criteria: AC-1: read project/backlog.json id orchestrator_interactive_dashboard_app IN FULL before doing anything else. It is the complete, Product-Owner-decided bounded spec (prior-art survey, recommended architecture, the AMENDMENT into a PO+Orchestrator workbench, and the final 'PO SCOPE BOUNDARY' section with IN SCOPE / DEFERRED lists). This SESSION_START does not restate it -- treat the IN SCOPE section as build-it and DEFERRED as report-if-tempted-via-RELAY_QUESTION, not as open questions for another design round.

AC-2: post one short technical-design RELAY_NOTE on this relay BEFORE writing any code, covering exactly three things the backlog note leaves as implementation detail: (a) the action-id registry design -- what identifies a registered relay-write action, how it stores the exact operation/argument-set/working-directory it resolves to, and how staleness is detected ('if the underlying command has changed since the id was issued, the stale approval must not apply'); (b) the relay-write schema each dashboard action appends -- RELAY_DECISION vs. a new lighter marker, justified against docs/design/LOCAL_RELAY_PROTOCOL.md's existing marker set (do not invent an incompatible file format); (c) the session-token + Origin/CSRF scheme for the localhost-bound server. Wait for a Product Owner acknowledgment RELAY_NOTE/RELAY_DECISION on this relay before proceeding past this note -- the same two-phase pattern relay/NXS-LOCAL-0007 itself used (design reviewed once, then implementation), except here the design is scoped to these three technical questions only, not the whole feature (already decided in the backlog note).

AC-3: once AC-2 is acknowledged, implement per the backlog note's IN SCOPE section: the five-section main screen (Awaiting you / Running movements / PO agenda / Integration queue / Recently completed), the six-tab detail panel (Summary / Live activity / Conversation / Changes / Evidence / History), movement cards with three distinct fields -- process status, work stage, last observed activity -- never inferred from git dirtiness alone and never a fabricated progress percentage, and the structured executable-request card (action id, exact operation, working directory, expected effect, blocker source, with the three-way routing: already-authorized -> auto-route to engineer with no PO question; genuinely new decision -> show and record to relay; platform/policy block -> show the real blocker, no button pretends to override it).

AC-4: read+relay-write only, as decided in the backlog note's scope boundary -- every card/button ends by appending to the movement's own relay file (a RELAY_DECISION, a queued note, or an equivalent structured instruction); the dashboard backend never executes git/gh/shell directly. 'Automatic routing of an already-authorized action' and a 'run this' button are the SAME mechanism (append the instruction to the relay so the next dispatch/resume picks it up) -- build it once.

AC-5: message-delivery UI copy defaults to 'Saved -> queued for next resume' as the normal, achievable outcome -- never implies a live session-control channel this repository does not have (orchestrator.py's --resume is a fresh respawn into the same worktree, not a reconnect to a running session -- relay/NXS-LOCAL-0015's own finding).

AC-6: reuse scripts/orchestrator.py's existing status-computation functions and scripts/local_relay.py directly -- no new scheduler, no new state model, no third-party/npm dependency; stdlib backend (http.server/wsgiref), vanilla JS frontend, bound to 127.0.0.1 only, matching relay/NXS-LOCAL-0013's own precedent.

AC-7: targeted tests for the new stage-derivation logic, the action-id registry/staleness check, and the config read/write endpoint, in isolation (no browser test harness needed -- test the data/API layer, same testing philosophy as relay/NXS-LOCAL-0013's own watch-loop tests).

AC-8: acceptance demonstration per the backlog note: track several concurrent movements through the UI, answer a pending design question through it, deliver a message to the correct worker, route an authorized command request through it, resume the affected work, open its produced UI -- without manual chat-to-chat copying or git commands. Record real command/UI evidence (screenshots or terminal output), not a description.

AC-9: validation and state: targeted tests green; because this is new scope touching scripts/orchestrator.py's status functions, run the full one-shot regression once (DEV.TEST.1); project-state bookkeeping in this PR.
